newsitem.title: USA: Ore. commission staff rejects Enron rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Ore. commission staff rejects Enron rate cut.

text.p: The staff of the Oregon Public Utility Commission (OPUC) said Tuesday it has rejected the latest rate cut offer from Enron Corp and Portland General Electric Co.
Enron and Portland announced last year plans to merge in a stock swap deal valued near $3.2 billion.

The deal has been approved by other government agencies, including the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, but the issue of a rate reduction for Oregon electricity customers has put a damper on clearance at the state level.

Commission staff said Tuesday they would recommend approval of the merger if the company is willing to credit Portland General customers $105 million for a period of time that is yet to be determined.
The staff had previously sought a rate cut of $189.6 million over four years, while the companies' last offer was $40 to $50 million.
"Given the tenor of discussions we've had with Enron and Portland General, we believe this proposal is fair and equitable to all sides," Phil Nyegaard, OPUC analyst, said.
He added OPUC staff has agreed in principle with Enron and Portland General not to pursue claims associated with future earnings by Enron's unregulated operations, should the merger be approved.
All sides in the proposed merger will meet again Wednesday morning in Salem.
